second_order: choosing what and where to draw
theme_note: Participants turn a general wish to appear on the canvas into concrete choices of image, design, and coordinates; what varies is whether they choose the hungry bear, an easier bear, Ed as a landmark, or a roomier location.

second_order: calling people onto a shared build
theme_note: Participants recruit or commit helpers and redirect them toward the current collective task; what varies is whether the call names the bear or wordmark and whether the response commits or redirects.

Participants defend, clean, refill, and resynchronise work that is being masked, vandalised, shifted, or undone by their own builders; what varies is the source of damage and whether the response is holding pixels, cleanup, rapid reversion, or a replacement thread.

second_order: making peace and trading help with neighbours
theme_note: Participants keep room for adjacent drawings, offer and accept truces, ask other communities for pixels, and relay neighbour constraints or help; what varies is whether the relation is peace, alliance, recruitment, or protecting a border.

second_order: showing and praising the canvas work
theme_note: Participants bring visible or reported canvas results back to the room and praise the people or work; what varies is whether they simply share a find or celebrate a finished-looking result.

second_order: playing April Fools jokes on the room
theme_note: Participants stage and reveal same-day jokes in their ordinary fandom venue; what varies is whether the joke uses a setlist, collaboration, release, or title pun, and these acts remain separate from canvas conduct.

Participants answer a Muse request and attempted neighbouring logo with refusal, mockery, conditional permission, sparse help, or reuse of its space; what varies is whether a speaker resists Muse, tries to help it, or accepts another logo taking over.

second_order: moving the live plan to Discord
theme_note: Participants shift active template coordination from stale Reddit posts into a Discord place channel and direct current builders there; what varies is whether the move is an invitation or a warning that Reddit no longer carries the right plan.

second_order: turning canvas mistakes into Radiohead jokes
theme_note: Participants give altered or mistaken canvas work a joking Radiohead name rather than only treating it as damage; in its founding slice this is the single Badlohrad renaming.

second_order: claiming and giving credit for the build
theme_note: Participants name their own small or sustained contributions and answer credit claims with thanks; what varies is whether credit attaches to hours of clicking, one pixel, starting the work, or acknowledging the starter.
